dimension_justifications.soundness: Within the explicitly stated count-exchangeable replay model, the posterior flip object and tower-property argument give a coherent conditional guarantee; this review did not independently audit every proof.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper states its replay, not-online-deployment scope unusually clearly, but the main-text related-work discussion is too compressed to make the novelty boundary immediately auditable.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The snapshot supports a distinct, useful package: a count-mixture posterior certificate for disagreement with a finite full-vote replay endpoint, selected-family calibration, and explicit shift/drift analyses. Its significance is narrow because the certificate is conditional on a specified replay model and does not establish online stopped-answer correctness or operational savings.

paper_summary: The paper models each task by a latent full-N binary pass count drawn from a mixture H, then stops when the posterior probability that the current prefix majority disagrees with the corresponding full-N majority is at most alpha. It augments this exact known-mixture replay certificate with FIT/CAL/TEST empirical-Bernstein/Bonferroni selection, fixed-rule total-variation analysis, and synthetic ordered-drift stress tests.
strongest_verified_contribution: A precisely scoped posterior conditional flip certificate for a specified count-exchangeable replay endpoint: under the frozen mixture model, any prefix-measurable rule that stops only at certified states has replay flip probability at most alpha without a union bound over stopping times.
strengths: The novelty claim is disciplined: the manuscript does not claim to be the first online early stopper and separates replay full-vote agreement from gold correctness, tokens, latency, and deployment order.

Against the source-verified positioning, BAYES-H has a clear structural distinction from ASC/ESC-style early stopping and MARS: sequential count-exchangeable replay, a posterior over finite task counts, and disagreement with the corresponding full-N vote.

Selected-family calibration and fixed-rule TV analysis make the proposed object more consequential than an oracle-prior observation, while TV robustness remains confined to mixture shift and synthetic results to named drift mechanisms.
The conformal and confidence-sequence contrast is appropriately narrow.
questions: Can the main paper add a compact source-supported comparison matrix for ASC, ESC, MARS, conformal prediction, and confidence sequences listing endpoint, information/order assumption, guarantee, and rule-selection control?

Which component is primary conceptual novelty: the finite-count mixture certificate, exact posterior stopping rule, selected-family calibration, or TV robustness functional? Please distinguish new derivations from standard empirical-Bernstein, Bonferroni, and LP ingredients.
Can the paper state alongside Proposition 1 that its robustness claim concerns distributional shift in the task-count mixture after freezing a rule, not chronological rollout dependence?

issues.location: Section 2, especially adaptive-sampling and conformal/anytime paragraphs; Sections 1 and 4 contribution statements
issues.observed_evidence: The source-verified closest-work matrix establishes narrow relationship sentences for ASC, ESC, MARS, conformal prediction, and confidence sequences. The manuscript gives only prose contrasts, without a common feature-level comparison of target event, rollout-order assumption, posterior/model assumption, stopping guarantee, and selection guarantee. Thus structural distinctness is supported in the replay setting, but the exact novelty boundary is not readily checkable.
issues.why_it_matters: A posterior conditional-probability stopping identity can appear close to several sequential-inference or early-stopping templates unless the distinct finite full-vote replay endpoint and count-mixture assumptions are compared directly. This does not assert external subsumption.
issues.required_fix: Move a concise source-supported comparison matrix into the main paper or appendix linked from Section 2. State that the contribution certifies a specified count-exchangeable full-vote replay endpoint, not general online early stopping, and retain present non-universal claims.
issues.verification_test: For every named neighbor, the matrix identifies endpoint, data/order model, guarantee type, and selection treatment; each relationship sentence is no stronger than bundled source-verified positioning.
issues.evidence_needed: A feature-level comparison backed by locked sources, or additional source verification if stronger distinctions are claimed.

issues.location: Sections 1 and 4--5, particularly contribution items 2--3, Theorem 2, Proposition 1, and Remark 3
issues.observed_evidence: The paper presents exact posterior certificate, empirical-Bernstein/Bonferroni calibration, finite breakpoint accounting, and fixed-rule TV maximization as one package, but does not sharply separate the conceptual novelty of the certificate object from standard calibration and optimization tools.
issues.why_it_matters: Without this separation, the contribution can read broader than source-verified positioning warrants. Identifying the new object and role of established tools would make the narrow significance more persuasive.
issues.required_fix: Add one paragraph naming the count-mixture posterior flip event and finite-replay consequence as the proposed object, while describing empirical-Bernstein/Bonferroni as calibration and TV maximization as fixed-rule robustness analysis; restate that neither yields arbitrary ordered-online validity.
issues.verification_test: The abstract, contribution list, and related-work comparison consistently distinguish the new formulation from established tools and do not imply online or universal robustness.

ethics_concerns: No novelty-specific ethics concern. The manuscript appropriately discloses that replay quantities are not deployment correctness or operational-cost measurements.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A source-verified feature-level positioning against named adjacent methods demonstrating the distinct endpoint and guarantee without overclaiming.
New ordered-online evidence with stopped-answer correctness and telemetry would materially expand significance, though it is not required for the present replay contribution.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Evidence that a cited neighbor already provides the same finite count-exchangeable posterior full-vote flip certificate with equivalent calibration and scope.
Evidence that replay assumptions, frozen-prior conditions, or selection boundaries are violated.
review_limitations: This assessment used only the frozen snapshot and bundled source-verified positioning; it did not conduct an external literature search or assert external subsumption.
